questions.q: What is a voice of customer tool for restaurants?
questions.a: It's software that gathers what guests say about you, from reviews and surveys to social posts, and analyzes it to show how they feel. The best tools go further than a sentiment score and explain why it moved and which locations drive it. That gives your team clear priorities for improving the guest experience.

questions.q: How do I choose a voice of customer tool for my restaurant group?
questions.a: Start by mapping every place guests leave feedback, since a tool that watches only one channel gives you a misleading picture. Then decide whether you mainly need to collect, analyze or act on feedback, and check that the tool connects to your POS, CRM or reservation data. For several locations, look for cross-location reporting, per-site drill-down and role-based access.

questions.q: What's the difference between a survey tool and a voice of customer platform?
questions.a: A survey tool collects structured answers to the questions you ask, while a voice of customer platform also pulls in unsolicited feedback like reviews and social comments. Some platforms only analyze open-ended feedback you already have and sit on top of your existing tools. Many restaurant groups combine surveys and reviews in one view to get a fuller picture.

questions.q: How can AI help with voice of customer analysis?
questions.a: AI reads open-ended reviews and survey answers at scale and sorts them into themes like food quality, wait time or staff friendliness. It can then track how sentiment for each theme changes by location and over time. At Momos, Alfie brings reviews into one place and replies to them, while Rockie surfaces sentiment trends and ranks locations so HQ knows where to focus.

questions.q: Is a voice of customer tool worth it for a small restaurant?
questions.a: It can be, as long as you pick something simple you'll actually use. Lightweight survey tools let independent restaurants start collecting satisfaction scores quickly without a long setup. As you add locations, you'll want a platform that compares sites and routes issues to the right manager.
